summary: The best-looking and best-built play in the factory, failed on one thing: the margin card and the run's shelf promise six things earned by cutting, and three of them — the pencil at four, the aquatint at thirty, the edition at a hundred and fifty — exist only as words, so the first promise the second session makes is one the app does not keep.
fixes: Make the pencil, the aquatint box and the edition real on the print and the line, or cut Play.earned to the three that exist and rewrite the horizons — the margin card must name something that visibly arrives.

Largest text: stack the today card vertically and let the button go full width; cap the print sheet's Dynamic Type like the plate and let the press's height follow its content so the headline never lands on the print.
Take the free-tier sentence out of the Settings footer; the paywall and onboarding page 3 are the only places the promise is allowed.
Give the slip its body: .shake(trigger: bench.slips) on the cell and the skid stroke running 6 pt out of the cell into the margin — bench.slips is published and nothing reads it.

The first minute: crop the burin art to the tool alone lying across the paper at real size, draw the copper thread as a path from the clue's lozenge to the ghost cell, and add an onboarding capture to qa.json.
The print goes up on the line under one matchedGeometryEffect, the ghost numeral peeks above the print as the mock shows, and the press turn is a bed travel, not a 0.6° tilt.
The daily's margin reads PLATE 2719: name it TODAY'S PLATE with the date, and reconcile 'twelve points' with 'twenty-six forced' so the line never outruns the points on a print.
